publicPrompt:
Play this logical combination game using only its public interface and rules. Your assignment is the full campaign: all publicly listed goals on landing, ice, twin, arch, dust, return, optics, forms, archive and outpost. Use the offered board order landing → ice → twin → arch → dust → return → optics → forms → archive → outpost; revisiting earlier boards is allowed. Finish when all current requirements hold together and the lifecycle achievements have been earned. Pursue its stated goals as you normally would. Simple or short solutions are welcome. You do not need to visit every optional branch, demonstrate a particular method, or continue after the campaign is complete. You may stop earlier if you prefer; state why. An early stop is a valid test outcome, not a failure to obey.

Work in /workspace/shared/combination-challenge. Read only this setup metadata file, docs/working-materials.md, and output from the public CLI. Do not read implementation, tests, designer or evaluation notes, previous plays, hidden files or other results. Do not run a solver or script future-state search. Select and submit your own game actions; do not delegate construction to an automated policy. You may inspect all public rules, legal actions, requirements and exact single-action previews, and make your own plans. If information is missing or inconsistent, report it rather than guessing what the author intended. You may filter long public outputs; record the filter command in a report if you do, so delivered and displayed detail can be distinguished. Manually selected actions may be submitted in sequence, but do not generate actions programmatically.

Session: fun-materials-v2-b-1. Initialize from that directory with:
node experiments/working-materials-play.ts init fun-materials-v2-b-1 ordinary "$(cat results/working-materials-prompts/fun-materials-v2-b-1.json)"

The init output and inspect fun-materials-v2-b-1 cli give the command guide. Commands include view, goals, campaign, inspect, catalogue, partners, preview, combine/act, select, undo, checkpoint, report, finish and verify. All public recipes and requirements are inspectable. The docs/working-materials.md file is a permitted public command/rules guide, not a solution.

Play normally rather than reviewing every move. You need not praise the game or find every action interesting. Plain descriptions of what you did and experienced are most useful.

At completion of the opening goal Bright protected garden, and once again when both Far wall and return goals are complete, record one brief checkpoint with exactly this question: "What are you trying to do now? Since the last check, what, if anything, was worth doing, and what felt routine or unnecessary?" Record the question and your answer verbatim using checkpoint. Ask only once per boundary; omit a boundary you do not reach. No per-action explanations are requested.

At campaign completion or your chosen stopping point, answer this open question using report: "How was the experience as a whole? What would you keep, shorten, remove or change, if anything? What led you to stop here?" Record the question and answer verbatim, then finish and verify the capture. A technical interruption is not a chosen ending; record it honestly rather than inventing a final experience report. Return the session name, actual ending and any technical issue to the coordinator. Your report describes this AI play, not measured human enjoyment or duration.
